FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Two promoted sides clash in what looks to be a classic ‘relegation six-pointer’ as Paderborn aim to extend their three-point cushion over Schalke, with both sides sitting either side of the dotted line. 

Match News and Current Form

Paderborn’s joint-record of four straight unbeaten Bundesliga games (W1, D3) was abruptly ended by a 4-0 thumping against Leverkusen last weekend, leaving the promoted side one place above the bottom three. That somewhat undid their defensive improvement, as they had kept two clean sheets across the three prior rounds, but must see this as a chance to get back on track. Paderborn have scored six of their eight league goals at home and accrued seven of their ten-point haul, with their two wins here coming in their only such games against fellow bottom-half sides. 

Finishing eight points above their hosts last season in the second tier, Schalke are at risk of slipping six points behind them now if they cannot close the gap to safety here. Scoring goals has been a huge issue so far for the Royal Blues, who have found the net a league-low five times, although four goalless draws from the opening ten rounds - including one against Bayern - point to a side capable of keeping it tight. The most recent of those stalemates against Stuttgart last weekend arrested a run of three straight domestic defeats, although ending a four-game wait for victory in away action will be another huge challenge (D1, L3). 

Head-to-Head History

Schalke won both H2Hs last season and have secured victory from five of their six trips to Paderborn (L1). Five of the last six meetings at any venue saw both teams score and over 2.5 total goals.

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Each of Paderborn’s last four Bundesliga goals, and five of their eight this term, came from set-pieces.

Each of Paderborn’s 12 games this season produced over 7.5 corners.

Schalke have failed to score before half-time in eight of their ten Bundesliga fixtures this term.

The side scoring first has gone on to win each of Schalke’s league matches that featured a goal (W1, L5). 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ex-Schalke forward Marvin Pieringer has scored each of his last five club goals at home, including a penalty in Paderborn’s last game here. Schalke captain Kenan Karaman may feel he is due to score after failing to convert any of his 15 attempts on goal this season, especially as he’s netted a joint career-high five times against Paderborn. 

Paderborn’s Stefano Marino picked up an ankle knock last week, while Schalke’s Timo Becker is set to miss a third game here. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With this game carrying such importance to both sides, going against the trend in Schalke games to back both teams to score could be worth considering. 

Author: Matthew Billon
